quests.doctorQuestion: Can you describe the pain in your shoulder and when it started?
options: It's a sharp, catching pain when I lift my arm overhead that started three days ago after tennis practice.
It just hurts really bad and I don't like it at all.
My shoulder feels funny sometimes, maybe for a few weeks or days.
quests.pitfallAvoided: Avoided vague descriptions and missing timeline details.
quests.explanation: Stating the exact sensation ('sharp, catching'), the precise motion trigger ('lifting arm overhead'), and clear timeline ('three days ago') gives the doctor actionable diagnostic data.
quests.instruction: Select the patient response that gives the most accurate clinical clarity.

quests.doctorQuestion: Do you have any allergies or adverse reactions to antibiotics?
options: I think medicine makes me tired sometimes.
Yes, I broke out in hives and facial swelling from Amoxicillin two years ago, so I avoid all penicillin derivatives.
No, I never take any pills unless someone tells me to.
quests.pitfallAvoided: Avoided dismissing drug allergy history or confusing side effects with true allergies.
quests.explanation: Clearly naming the specific medication ('Amoxicillin'), the allergic manifestation ('hives and facial swelling'), and the drug family ('penicillin') prevents life-threatening prescribing errors.
quests.instruction: Select the patient response that gives the most accurate clinical clarity.

quests.doctorQuestion: How severe is your headache on a scale from 1 to 10, and what does it feel like?
options: It's about a 7; it's a tight, band-like dull pressure wrapping around my entire forehead with no nausea.
It's probably an 11 or 12, it's the worst thing ever in human history.
I don't know numbers, it's just a regular headache.
quests.pitfallAvoided: Avoided unrealistic hyperbolic ratings and unhelpful vagueness.
quests.explanation: A calibrated rating (7/10) paired with anatomical description ('tight, band-like dull pressure wrapping around forehead') and negative symptom rule-out ('no nausea') accurately points to tension-type cephalalgia.
quests.instruction: Select the patient response that gives the most accurate clinical clarity.

quests.doctorQuestion: Have you been taking any over-the-counter medication for this fever?
options: I took some random pills from my friend's cabinet yesterday.
I've taken 500mg of Acetaminophen every 6 hours since yesterday morning, which brings it down from 102°F to 99.5°F.
I don't believe in medicine so I just drink hot water.
quests.pitfallAvoided: Avoided unidentified medication ingestion and missing dosage logs.
quests.explanation: Providing exact medication names ('Acetaminophen'), precise dosage ('500mg every 6 hours'), and recorded temperature response demonstrates high medical communication clarity.
quests.instruction: Select the patient response that gives the most accurate clinical clarity.

quests.doctorQuestion: Does the back pain radiate anywhere, like down your legs?
options: Yes, it shoots down my left thigh and into my calf, especially when I sit down.
My whole body hurts everywhere all the time.
I don't understand what radiate means.
quests.pitfallAvoided: Avoided generalized complaints that obscure localized radiculopathy.
quests.explanation: Confirming distal radiation along a specific pathway ('shoots down left thigh into calf') alerts the physician to possible lumbar nerve root compression (sciatica).
quests.instruction: Select the patient response that gives the most accurate clinical clarity.
